I1.quote: The H2 storage capacities were measured using the Micromeritics ASAP2020 plus instrument. ACs were evacuated to an ultrahigh vacuum at 300 °C for 12 h before starting the measurement.

I2.quote: In this study, heteroatom (O, N)-doped activated carbon (AC) is produced using urea and KOH activation from abundant and cost-effective biomass waste for H2 storage.
I2.location: main, p. 1, Abstract; carbon content of the measured ACs 81.93-88.36% C in main, p. 5, Table 1 (% components, C)

I3.quote: The O and N co-doped AC exhibits the highest specific surface area and H2 storage capacity (2.62 wt%), increasing by 47% from unmodified AC at −196 °C and 1 bar.
I3.location: main, p. 1, Abstract (also Table 1, p. 5, and Fig. 9, p. 7)

I4.quote: Additionally, the specific surface area and pore volume were developed and increased up to 1118 m2 g−1 and 0.577 cm3 g−1 respectively.
I4.location: main, p. 4, Section 3.1 (Characterization); SBET per sample in main, p. 5, Table 1

I5.quote: In this study, heteroatom (O, N)-doped activated carbon (AC) is produced using urea and KOH activation from abundant and cost-effective biomass waste for H2 storage.

notes: Own H2 isotherms at -196 and 25 °C up to 1 bar for five jujube-branch ACs (N-AC900-2, N-AC900-1, N-AC800-1, AC900, AC800) on a Micromeritics ASAP2020 plus (the paper does not use the word 'volumetric'); 1-bar values in Table 1 rows marked 'The present work', isotherms in Fig. 9a,b. Other Table 1 rows (refs 11-66) are literature values, not this paper's measurements. GCMC simulations are additional, not the only uptake data. SBET by multipoint BET from N2 at -196 °C (Section 2.1.2), per sample in Table 1, on the same samples whose H2 uptake is measured. Majority component carbon: 81.93-88.36 wt% C by CHN analysis (Table 1). No retraction notice; no statement that the H2 data were published before; not a review or thesis.
